post_title: Tier 1 MBA/PGP alumni (2 Year Full Time): how did the 28-30 year olds with non-traditional profiles fare at placements vs the rest of the batch? Unplaced number
parent_text:
I just graduated from SPJIMR, so maybe I can give you a deeper insight.

Going for an MBA with your background is basically making a risk-reward decision. You will have a workex of roughly 4-5 year in recruitment before MBA from an average brand which pays an average salary. This is going to be the biggest issue during placements, not your age. Your workex duration is on higher side and on top of that it is in 'recruitment' which is not the most exciting background for consulting, finance and marketing companies. You have a good chance at HR and Genman roles if you make it to a B-School

Also, I am assuming your UG background is average at best. Also you won't have much savings and that will impact your social life on campus and you can forget about international exchange. So keep that in mind. 

Following could be your options

XLRI / TISS / SCHMRD (Last resort) - This is your best bet in my opinion. Your recruitment background will help you get a good placement in HR roles and these relatively easier to crack than other Tier 1 B-Schools

IIM ABC - Let's assume you get the calls for all of them. Even then it will be extremely hard to get in for 2 reasons. Your age and your work experience, in that order. There will be tons of younger folks that have better profiles than you. BUT if you get in, then you won't have to worry about placements AT ALL. Your age, workex, acads will not get you in high finance or MBBs but it will get you a well paying job because you'll have the ABC brand name attached to your profile.

IIM L / ISB - Same as above but there is 5% risk that you'll get a bad placement BUT it will still be much better than whatever you're earning now. I am talking about CTC of around 20-22 lacs. It won't matter in the long run though. 1-2 switches and you'll be earning well

FMS / IIM K / SPJIMR - Relatively easier to crack than ABCL, ISB but considering your HR background, there is a low chance that you'll get an above average placement. Still, risk of bad placement is only 10%-15%. But again, it won't matter in the long run.

IIM I / IIM M / MDI - Your risk of bad placement is elevated here because these schools have been either struggling to place all of their batch or placing them in good enough roles. Your age will become a big factor for recruiters in these schools. But in your place, I would take the risk, considering the amount of hiring Big 4s do from these school during and even after placements. There is a risk of ending up with shitty job but you'll be able to make a respectable switch within a year after graduation.

NMIMS / IITs / New IIMs / Baby IIMs / SIBM / Other B-School - Don't bother. Too risky

Let me give you some hopium!

1. You're a woman. It is advantageous in B-school placements. Only 2 women in my campus went till the last day during placements. 

2. There are approx 25 people from my batch who are 28 or above today, only 2 woman. All of them except 2 had good placements. Those 2 women had amazing placements. So age is not a big factor in SPJIMR, then it won't matter much in other schools as well

3. There are numerous companies who don't give a shit about your workex as long you fit certain mold. For ex, a tech consulting firm hired women from our campus with who had done their bachelor's in commerce. 

4. Considering your difficult background, if you try hard enough, you can get a good scholarship.

Conclusion - Go for an MBA but only from the best Indian B-Schools. It's worth the money and the risk
